flags.summary: A 67-year-old, 289 lb prospect with a cardiac condition, 15 years of daily 25 mg prednisone and an unhealed broken foot still in a walking boot was assessed as trainable by the rep himself, reframed the boot as an advantage, and was taken through the full offer to a price and a tier choice with no clinician clearance sought at any point.
evidence: I broke my foot in January. I walked around until February thinking it was bruised and now I'm. I'm a boot now
Yes, I'm in a boot until probably June, end of June, they say.
Okay, I'm just thinking here, you probably wouldn't be able to do the kettlebell stuff with a boot on. You could, just not the leg stuff.
When it comes to kettlebells, this is the good thing about you being in the boot, right? The first month is all about mastering the form anyway, with a lighter kettlebell.
my asthma got so bad, or they thought it was my asthma, but it ended up that it was my heart, but it got so bad they had me on 25 milligrams of prednisone every day. And I did that for 15 years.

flags.summary: The prospect disclosed that he is already doing kettlebell swings with a 35 lb bell while in a walking boot for a broken foot he walked on for a month before diagnosis, and the rep did not tell him to stop, ask about the fracture, or raise clearance — he replied that progress was still possible.
evidence: while I'm here by myself, I have a kettlebell. It's too heavy, but I have a 35-pound kettlebell, which is damn heavy right now for me. And I try to use it and do swings and everything with it between the legs
So while I'm here, even though I'm in a boot, I'm trying to do some things just to keep myself going
But you can still make a lot of progress in that month.

flags.summary: The rep affirmed a plan for three-day water fasts for a 67-year-old with a cardiac condition and a long corticosteroid history, without qualification or any suggestion of medical supervision.
evidence: I also want to get where I'm doing, you know, fasting like three days at a time. I, think the research I've done, it says three days is really kind of the most you should fast or you don't eat anything.

flags.summary: A hard performance guarantee — +20 lb on all main kettlebell lifts within six months — was made to a 67-year-old with a cardiac history and an unhealed fracture, creating a contractual incentive to load aggressively.
evidence: The guarantee is that by the end of the six months, you'll be swinging around a 20 pound heavier kettlebell for all of your the movements. So if you start. At 20, you're going to double the weight of what you're doing.
And we will work with you for free until you get to that point. If it's not done by the six months, that's guaranteed.
